title_en: Xuzhou Dashun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Wang Zhiqiang — dispute over a commercial housing pre-sale contract
ruling_gist_en: A real estate development enterprise, for the purpose of evading the state's regulation of the real estate industry, signs a false commercial housing sales contract with a third party in the name of that party, and mortgages the property to obtain bank credit funds. If the buyer of the commercial housing knew that the contract did not reflect the true intention of both parties, then such circumstances fall within the provision of Article 52(3) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and the contract shall be determined to be void.

full_text_en:
Xuzhou Dashun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Wang Zhiqiang — dispute over pre-sale contract of commercial housing

Ruling Summary

If a real estate development enterprise, for the purpose of evading the state's regulation and control of the real estate industry, enters into a false commercial housing sales contract with itself in another person's name to obtain bank credit funds by mortgage, and the commercial housing buyer is fully aware that the contract does not reflect the true intent of both parties, then such circumstances fall within the provisions of Article 52(3) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and the contract shall be found invalid.

Plaintiff: Xuzhou Dashun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Jiahe Street, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal representative: Yan Changyin, General Manager of the Company.

Defendant: Wang Zhiqiang, male, 63 years old, Han ethnicity, retired cadre, residing in Yunhe Town, Pizhou City, Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiff, Xuzhou Dashun Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dashun Company), initiated an action in the Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant, Wang Zhiqiang, regarding a dispute over a pre-sale contract of commercial housing.

The plaintiff, Dashun Company, alleged: For the purpose of corporate financing, the plaintiff intended to obtain bank loans for temporary corporate use by entering into false commercial housing sales contracts, and to repay the loans in full to the bank when the company had sufficient funds. The defendant (a relative of the plaintiff's employee and legal representative, Yan Changyin), Wang Zhiqiang, agreed and signed the contract in his own name. The housing price and interest were borne by the plaintiff, the obtained bank loan was used by the plaintiff, and the plaintiff owned the housing ownership. On April 2, 2008, the plaintiff and the defendant entered into a false "Commercial Housing Sales Contract", which provided that the plaintiff would sell to the defendant the unit 1701, Building 1, Shunhe Gongyu Comprehensive Building, located at Jiahe Street, developed by the plaintiff, at a total price of RMB 1,060,000, with payment by mortgage loan. A down payment of RMB 318,000 was to be paid on April 2, 2008, and the remaining balance of RMB 742,000 was to be paid in full before April 13, 2008. After the contract was signed, the plaintiff paid the down payment and relevant deed tax. On April 23, 2008, with the defendant's cooperation, a bank mortgage loan was processed in the defendant's name. The loan proceeds were used by the plaintiff, and the monthly bank loan repayments were made by the plaintiff, all without objection from the defendant. On August 19, 2009, the plaintiff sold the disputed property, which was in the defendant's name but actually owned by the plaintiff, to the buyer Zhao Jing. The contract provided that Zhao Jing would first pay the plaintiff RMB 390,000, and from August 19, 2009, the outstanding loan balance would be borne by Zhao Jing, with the property rights belonging to Zhao Jing. Zhao Jing continued to repay the loan until March 2012, all without objection from the defendant. On April 20, 2012, when Zhao Jing went to make a repayment, she was informed that the loan account had been closed by the defendant. To protect its legitimate rights and interests, the plaintiff requested the court to confirm that the commercial housing sales contract signed by the plaintiff and the defendant on April 2, 2008, was invalid; to order the defendant, upon the date of full repayment of the mortgage loan on the disputed property, to cooperate in canceling the mortgage registration on the disputed property; and to restore the registered owner of the disputed property to the plaintiff's name.

The plaintiff, Dashun Company, submitted the following evidence:

1. The plaintiff's business license and organization code certificate, proving the plaintiff's proper legal standing.

2. A copy of the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" dated April 2, 2008, signed by the plaintiff (Dashun Company) and the defendant (Wang Zhiqiang); a copy of the real estate mortgage contract dated April 24, 2008; and originals of the down payment receipt, sales invoice, the deed tax payment certificate issued by Xuzhou Municipal Finance Bureau on April 7, 2008, the property maintenance fund payment voucher issued by Xuzhou Municipal Property Maintenance Fund on April 8, 2008, and the ownership registration fee receipts issued by the Property Management Office of Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau on April 15 and April 29, 2008. These documents proved that the plaintiff, in order to obtain a bank loan, entered into a false commercial housing sales contract with the defendant on April 2, 2008, but the defendant did not actually perform the obligations under the commercial housing sales contract.

3. A copy of the "House Sale Contract" dated August 19, 2009, signed by the plaintiff (Dashun Company, Party A) and Zhao Jing (Party B); and a written statement by Zhao Jing dated April 20, 2012, proving that on August 19, 2009, the plaintiff had sold the disputed property to the actual buyer, Zhao Jing, and that from August 19, 2009, Zhao Jing had been making monthly repayments on the bank loan for the disputed property.

4. A detailed bank deposit record for the account in the name of Wang Zhiqiang, account number 1251019980110795143, from May 2008 to March 2012; and a set of bank deposit slips from February 2011 to August 2011, proving that the bank loan for the disputed property was repaid by the plaintiff (Dashun Company) from May 2008 to August 2009, and from September 2009, the loan was repaid by the actual buyer, Zhao Jing, by transfer. The defendant had deposited RMB 5,000 in cash into the account in July 2011 but withdrew that RMB 5,000 on July 18, 2011.

5. A copy of the passbook in the name of Wang Zhiqiang, opened on April 22, 2008 (original handed to the bank); the original passbook in the name of Wang Zhiqiang, renewed on August 25, 2010; a set of customer receipts for deposit slips from August 2011 to March 2012; and a written statement by Zhang, the accountant of the plaintiff (Dashun Company), proving that the bank loan for the disputed property was repaid monthly by the plaintiff and the actual buyer. The original passbook showed that the magnetic stripe was re-encoded on August 23, 2010, and that such re-encoding was done with the defendant's consent, indicating the defendant was aware that he was not performing the mortgage loan contract.

6. Partial salary records of the defendant (Wang Zhiqiang) at Xuzhou Dashun Environmental Protection Building Materials Co., Ltd.; and the business license of Xuzhou Dashun Environmental Protection Building Materials Co., Ltd., proving that the defendant was an employee of a company controlled by Yan Changyin, the legal representative of the plaintiff (Dashun Company).

7. A copy of the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" (Contract No. NO.0049275) dated April 8, 2007, signed by Dashun Company (seller, plaintiff) and Wang Zhiqiang (buyer, defendant), proving that the defendant had previously purchased a house at Qianxin New Village from the plaintiff on April 8, 2007. Therefore, the disputed property was not truly intended to be sold to the defendant by the plaintiff, and this did not affect the defendant's exercise of first-home buyer rights.

8. Five copies of "Commercial Housing Sales Contracts" dated April 2, 2008, signed by the plaintiff (Dashun Company) as seller with buyers Yan Yan, Zhang Liyun, Yan Lei, Li Demin, and Liu Dong; consecutive receipts numbered 7000761-7000767 and a loan schedule; a copy of the real estate mortgage contract dated April 24, 2008, signed by mortgagor Xu Binlin with the Xuzhou Branch of Agricultural Bank of China, with property at Shunhe Gongyu 2-1702 as collateral; and originals of the house property certificates and land use certificates of Yan Yan, Liu Dong, and Zhang Liyun. This evidence proved that on April 2, 2008, the plaintiff entered into false commercial housing sales contracts with the defendant and the aforementioned persons to obtain bank loans. The house property certificates and land use certificates of some of these persons were held by the plaintiff. The defendant (Wang Zhiqiang) took the documents required for property registration, claiming his child needed them for school in Xuzhou, obtained the house property certificate and land use certificate, but did not return the originals to the plaintiff.

9. Witness testimony from Li Demin, who appeared in court and testified: "My wife is the sister of Yan Changyin, the legal representative of Dashun Company. My wife asked me to help. Dashun Company used my name to register property and obtain a loan from the bank. The loan was used by Dashun Company, and Dashun Company made monthly repayments to the bank. I only signed documents and did not ask about other matters. When the contract was signed, I heard that Wang Zhiqiang also came, but we did not know each other, so we did not speak. After retirement, I worked as the property manager at Dashun Company."

The defendant, Wang Zhiqiang, argued: The plaintiff's allegations do not conform to the facts.

1. Regarding the intent behind signing the contract: Before October 2009, the defendant was not an employee of the plaintiff (Dashun Company) and was not aware of the plaintiff's urgent need for funds. It was impossible for him to voluntarily offer to sign a false contract in his own name to obtain bank funds. The defendant had intended to buy a house in Xuzhou around 2007. The plaintiff's legal representative and executive director were both relatives of the defendant, and the plaintiff was a family enterprise. Therefore, based on mutual convenience and benefit, the defendant reserved a house of about 100 square meters at the plaintiff's premises. However, that house was later sold by the plaintiff to someone else. Upon the plaintiff's recommendation, the defendant signed a formal house sale contract on April 2, 2008, and ordered the disputed property. Subjectively, the defendant never agreed with the plaintiff to enter into a false contract. The commercial housing sales contract, the subsequent bank loan contract, and the mortgage contract all reflected the defendant's true intent.

2. Regarding the down payment and bank loan repayment: When the contract was signed, it was agreed that the down payment of RMB 318,000 would be paid by the defendant, but this amount was first borrowed from the defendant's uncle, Yan Changyin, the executive director of the plaintiff. It was also agreed that the bank loan repayments before the delivery of the property and the upfront certificate fees would be paid by the plaintiff on the defendant's behalf, to be settled together upon property delivery. After the contract was signed, the defendant repeatedly demanded delivery of the property, but the plaintiff delayed on various pretexts. The defendant did not remain silent; rather, the defendant was in a weak position in the house purchase contract and was unwilling to have a falling out with relatives or engage in litigation, resulting in repeated infringements of the defendant's interests.

3. Regarding the secondary sale to Zhao Jing: According to the plaintiff's complaint, the plaintiff unilaterally sold the disputed property a second time to Zhao Jing on August 19, 2009. However, the defendant was unaware of this until the end of 2010, when the repayment passbook was demagnetized and needed replacement. Only then did the defendant learn from the plaintiff's staff that his house had been resold and that the bank loan was already being repaid by Zhao Jing. The defendant was very upset and immediately approached Yan Changyin, demanding performance of the contract and settlement for the property to take possession. At the defendant's repeated insistence, the plaintiff agreed in June 2011 to perform the contract and processed the property title documents in the defendant's name. The defendant also reported the loss of the repayment passbook and changed the password in July 2011, intending to repay the bank loan directly by himself. However, shortly thereafter, the plaintiff changed its mind again. The defendant had no choice but to change the bank repayment account in February 2012 to repay the bank loan, and in May 2012 sent a letter to the plaintiff demanding performance of the contract. If this were a false contract, it would deprive the defendant of substantial substantive interests. If, as the plaintiff claims, the contract was a false contract entered into for the purpose of obtaining bank loans by fraud, this might involve a criminal offense. In that case, the present civil proceedings should be stayed, and the case referred to the public security authorities for handling.

The defendant, Wang Zhiqiang, submitted the following evidence:

1. Original of the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" (Contract No. NO.0130315) dated April 2, 2008, signed by Dashun Company (seller, plaintiff) and Wang Zhiqiang (buyer, defendant); a copy of the real estate mortgage contract dated April 24, 2008; and a copy of the loan contract. These documents proved that after mutual agreement, the plaintiff and defendant signed the commercial housing sales contract, which was registered and filed. The defendant mortgaged the disputed property to China Construction Bank and signed a loan contract. The loan proceeds of RMB 742,000 were paid to the plaintiff as the house purchase price.

2. Fourteen copies of materials submitted during the bank mortgage loan processing, showing that the defendant, as a first-time home buyer, received a 15% discount on the interest rate, obtaining a significant concession. This proved the defendant's genuine intention to purchase the house.

3. Original of the house property certificate for the disputed property (Xufangquanzheng Quanshanzi No. 156752) and original of the land use certificate [Xutuguoyong (2011) No. 29338], proving that the commercial housing sales contract signed by both parties was true and valid, and that the disputed property now belonged to the defendant (Wang Zhiqiang).

4. A receipt for the passbook loss reporting fee dated July 7, 2011; a copy of the passbook opened on February 9, 2012; and a letter dated May 2, 2012, proving that the defendant (Wang Zhiqiang) had been directly making bank loan repayments since February 2012 and had demanded in a letter dated May 2, 2012, that the plaintiff (Dashun Company) perform the contract and deliver the house as soon as possible.

5. Two stamped copies of the Xuzhou House Ownership Registration Review Form; an original of the sales invoice for the certificate-issuing purpose; an original of the mapping fee invoice; an original of the ownership registration fee receipt; two copies of the land registration application; a copy of the land use rights subdivision transfer certificate; a copy of the change application; and an original of the land registration fee receipt. These documents proved that the house property certificate and land use certificate were processed around June 2011, with the plaintiff (Dashun Company) agreeing to continue performing the contract and providing relevant materials to assist the defendant (Wang Zhiqiang) in the registration, rather than the defendant borrowing the documents from the plaintiff as alleged.

The Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province, found from the trial of first instance:

On April 2, 2008, the plaintiff (Dashun Company) and the defendant (Wang Zhiqiang) signed a commercial housing sales contract, which provided that the commercial housing purchased by Wang Zhiqiang was Unit 1701, Building 1, Shunhe Gongyu Comprehensive Building (building area 171.14 square meters). The unit price of the commercial housing was RMB 6,193.76 per square meter, with a total price of RMB 1,060,000, including a down payment of RMB 318,000 and a remaining balance of RMB 742,000 to be paid in full before April 13, 2008. The three-part down payment receipt was kept by the plaintiff. On April 7, 2008, the Xuzhou Municipal Finance Bureau issued a deed tax payment certificate in the name of Wang Zhiqiang for an amount of RMB 42,400; on April 8, 2008, the Xuzhou Municipal Property Maintenance Fund issued a property maintenance fund payment voucher in the name of Wang Zhiqiang for an amount of RMB 7,695; on April 15 and April 29, 2008, the Property Management Office of Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau issued ownership registration fee receipts for an amount of RMB 160. All the above fees were paid by the plaintiff, and the plaintiff held the originals of the payment vouchers.

On April 24, 2008, the defendant (Wang Zhiqiang) as borrower, the plaintiff (Dashun Company) as guarantor, and the Xuzhou Branch of China Construction Bank Co., Ltd. signed a "Real Estate Mortgage Contract", providing that the defendant (Wang Zhiqiang) would mortgage his property, located at Unit 1701, Building 1, Shunhe Gongyu Comprehensive Building, Xuzhou, to obtain a loan of RMB 742,000 from the bank, at a 15% discounted interest rate, for a term from April 24, 2008, to April 24, 2024. After the mortgage loan was disbursed, the plaintiff made monthly bank loan repayments at the agreed amount to the account in the name of Wang Zhiqiang, account number 125101998110795143.

On August 19, 2009, the plaintiff (Dashun Company) and a third party, Zhao Jing, signed a house sale contract, selling Unit 1701, Building 1, Shunhe Gongyu Comprehensive Building to Zhao Jing at a price of RMB 1,010,000. From that date, the bank loan for the disputed property was repaid by Zhao Jing.

On June 27, 2011, the Property Management Office of Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau issued an ownership registration fee receipt for an amount of RMB 80; Xuzhou Hongwei Surveying and Mapping Company issued a mapping fee invoice for an amount of RMB 20. On the same day, the defendant (Wang Zhiqiang) obtained the house property certificate (Xufangquanzheng Quanshanzi No. 156752), which indicated a building area of 171.66 square meters; on June 29, 2011, the Xuzhou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources issued a land registration fee receipt for an amount of RMB 18. On the same day, the defendant obtained the state-owned land use certificate (Xutuguoyong (2011) No. 29338). The originals of the above fee vouchers, the house property certificate, and the land use certificate were held by the defendant.

On July 7, 2011, the defendant (Wang Zhiqiang) deposited RMB 5,000 into the loan account for the disputed property, but withdrew the same amount on July 18, 2011. In February 2012, Wang Zhiqiang reported the loss of the original repayment passbook. On March 20, 2012, Zhao Jing repaid RMB 5,600 through a CCB ATM. After March 21, 2012, the bank loan for the disputed property was repaid by the defendant.

Separately found: On April 2, 2008, the plaintiff (Dashun Company) signed commercial housing sales contracts respectively with the defendant (Wang Zhiqiang) and with Yan Yan, Zhang Liyun, Yan Lei, Li Demin, Xu Binlin, Liu Dong, and others, with contract numbers No. 0130312-No. 0130318. The originals of the above sales contracts and the down payment and other documents necessary for processing relevant certificates were held by the plaintiff. The defendant's contract number was NO.0130315.

Further found: The defendant (Wang Zhiqiang) was formerly the political instructor of the Water Police Brigade of Pizhou Public Security Bureau, and took a second-line position in September 2009. From October 2009 to January 2012, the defendant worked at Xuzhou Dashun Environmental Protection Building Materials Co., Ltd., which is a corporate enterprise controlled by Yan Changyin, the legal representative of the plaintiff (Dashun Company).

The disputed issues in this case were: 1. Whether, at the time of signing the commercial housing sales contract, both parties knew it did not reflect their true intent; and 2. Whether the commercial housing sales contract in this case was valid.

The Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province, held in the first instance:

1. Both the plaintiff and the defendant were aware at the time of signing the commercial housing sales contract that the contract did not represent the true intent of either party. In this case, the plaintiff and defendant do not dispute the fact that they signed the commercial housing sales contract on April 2, 2008. The plaintiff, Dashun Company, claims that the contract was signed with the defendant, Wang Zhiqiang, for the purpose of obtaining a bank loan by using the defendant's name, and that the defendant was aware of this. The defendant claims that the contract was signed as a true expression of intent to purchase the property. The dispute centers on whether the defendant knew at the time of signing that the contract did not reflect the true intent of both parties. The court holds that, on the one hand, after the contract was signed, the down payment for the property was paid by the plaintiff. Subsequently, the plaintiff also paid, in the defendant's name, RMB 42,400 in deed tax, RMB 7,695 in property maintenance funds, and RMB 160 in ownership registration fees. Therefore, it should be determined that the defendant knew at the time of signing that he did not need to perform the contract and did not intend to actually perform it. On the other hand, on April 24, 2008, the plaintiff and defendant, as guarantor and borrower respectively, signed a "Real Estate Mortgage Loan Contract" with the Xuzhou Branch of China Construction Bank Corporation, using the property in question as collateral. Thereafter, the defendant also failed to repay the loan as agreed; instead, the plaintiff repaid it in the defendant's name. Although the defendant once deposited RMB 5,000 into the loan account for the property on July 7, 2011, he withdrew it immediately and did not repay the loan before March 20, 2012. Although the defendant claims that he requested the plaintiff to deliver the property and had a dispute with Yan Changyin, and that he obtained the ownership certificate and land use certificate for the property in June 2011, during this process, he neither paid the purchase price to the plaintiff nor claimed repayment of the housing loan. Furthermore, on April 2, 2008, the plaintiff signed a total of seven "Commercial Housing Sales Contracts" with contract numbers No. 0130312 to No. 0130318 with seven individuals, including the defendant Wang Zhiqiang, Yan Yan, Zhang Liyun, Yan Lei, Li Demin, Xu Binlin, and Liu Dong. The contract in Wang Zhiqiang's name, numbered NO.0130315, was among them. Based on the submitted evidence and testimony from witnesses who appeared in court, the property ownership certificates and land use certificates of Yan Yan, Liu Dong, and Zhang Liyun remain with the plaintiff; the loan of Xu Binlin is being repaid by the plaintiff; and Li Demin clearly stated that he only signed the contract and the loan repayment documents at the request of his wife (Yan Changyin's sister). None of the aforementioned signatories expressed any intent to assert rights over the properties specified in the contracts. Therefore, in summary, it should be determined that the defendant was aware that the plaintiff was using his name to sign the commercial housing sales contract for the transfer of ownership, which was not for the parties' true purpose.

2. The commercial housing sales contract in this case shall be found invalid. A contract is an agreement between natural persons, legal persons, or other organizations as equal parties for the establishment, modification, or termination of civil rights and obligations. When entering into a contract, parties shall not only follow the principles of voluntariness, fairness, compensation for equal value, and good faith, but also comply with laws and administrative regulations, respect social ethics, and shall not disrupt the socioeconomic order or harm the public interest. In this case, because the plaintiff and defendant used the signing of the commercial housing sales contract as a pretext to conceal their purpose of illegally obtaining bank credit funds by mortgaging the property with a bank loan, the contract shall be held invalid according to Article 52, Item (3) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. Property obtained by the parties as a result of the contract shall be returned. Therefore, the property in question remains owned by the plaintiff. The plaintiff shall reimburse the defendant for the loan payments made by the defendant after March 21, 2012. However, the defendant has not provided evidence in this case to prove the amount of loan payments he has made and has not made a claim for reimbursement. Therefore, the court will not address this issue in this case, and the parties may resolve it separately.

In conclusion, in accordance with Articles 5, 6, 7, 52(3), 56, and 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the Quanshan District People's Court of Xuzhou rendered the following judgment on December 25, 2012:

1. The "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" numbered NO.0130315 signed between the plaintiff, Dashun Company, and the defendant, Wang Zhiqiang, on April 2, 2008, is void;

2. The defendant, Wang Zhiqiang, shall, within ten days from the date the mortgage loan on the property is fully repaid, assist the plaintiff, Dashun Company, in canceling the property mortgage registration and assist the plaintiff, Dashun Company, in registering the property ownership.

Wang Zhiqiang, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court. Because Wang Zhiqiang failed to pay the appeal fee within the prescribed period, the Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court issued a civil ruling on May 13, 2013 (Xu Min Su Zhong Zi No. 0006): the case is deemed to have been withdrawn automatically upon appeal.
